27 What could describe the time-base of a cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO)?
A
the frequency per division on the screen
B
the number of divisions on the screen per unit frequency
C
the number of divisions on the screen per unit time
D
the time per division on the screen

hints: Notice the question asks about the time-base, which controls the horizontal x-axis sweep of the CRO spot.
Recall that the horizontal length of one cycle on screen multiplied by the time-base setting gives the period $T$.
Check the units: compare time per division such as $\text{s div}^{-1}$ with divisions per time or anything involving frequency per division.
walkthrough: Identify that the CRO screen has a vertical y-gain in $\text{V div}^{-1}$ and a horizontal time-base that moves the spot steadily across the x-axis.
State the rule: the time-base setting tells you how much time each horizontal division represents, for example $2.0 \text{ ms}$ per $1 \text{ div}$.
Use it to find time intervals: measured time $=$ number of horizontal divisions $\times$ time per division.
In particular, period $T = x \times$ time-base, where $x$ is the divisions for one complete wave, then frequency $= 1/T$.
Options A and B describe frequency per division or divisions per frequency, which confuses the derived quantity frequency with the set horizontal scale.
Option C describes divisions per unit time, which is the reciprocal with units $\text{div s}^{-1}$ instead of $\text{s div}^{-1}$. This is option D

A.explanation: Time-base does not set frequency per division. Frequency is $1/T$ and is found after measuring period, not set directly by the horizontal control.

B.explanation: This inverts the control to divisions per unit frequency. The CRO time-base dial is calibrated in time units such as $\text{ms div}^{-1}$, not divisions per hertz.

C.explanation: This is the reciprocal of the time-base. Divisions per unit time would have units $\text{div s}^{-1}$, whereas the control sets seconds per division.

D.explanation: The time-base sets the horizontal scale, so each horizontal division represents a fixed time such as $5.0 \text{ ms div}^{-1}$.
